title: Tri-deck 90′ Luxury Motor Yacht: Design & Layout
description: 90ft tri-deck luxury motor yacht: 23.5ft beam, three-level layout, premium amenities, twin MAN V12 power and advanced navigation—ideal for cruising or entertaining.
html:
This 90‑foot tri‑deck motor yacht pairs a flowing exterior profile with an interior volume maximized by a 23.5‑foot beam and an overall length of 88.92 ft, providing a three‑level arrangement that emphasizes visibility and social spaces; generous salon windows and an upper‑deck sky lounge create layered living areas that work equally well for extended cruising or weekend entertaining, while the hydraulically lifting bathing platform (750 kg capacity) and retractable passerelle simplify tender operations and water access.

Spacious Interior Volume and Main Salon Amenities

The main salon features oak wood flooring with inset carpet, a modular club sofa, two armchairs, a coffee table and a formal dining table for eight, all arranged around a Samsung 65″ QLED 4K TV with Apple TV and AirPlay 2 and a high‑fidelity Sonance/Sonos sound system; practical touches include sliding companionway doors, full‑height side window curtains, LED overhead lighting with dimmable Vimar switching, a day head and direct circulation to the galley and aft deck for effortless guest flow.

Gourmet Galley, Dining Areas and Alfresco Spaces

The galley is specified for serious onboard provisioning and service with integrated Frigoboat refrigeration (250L fridge/120L freezer) plus an MS130 drawer fridge, Miele appliances (dishwasher, oven, microwave), a 34‑bottle wine cooler and an Elica Nikola Tesla Prime induction hob with integrated extraction; dining options include the formal main‑deck table and multiple alfresco venues — a shaded aft deck with electrically operated sunbeds and privacy screen, and a flybridge aft wetbar with BBQ, ice maker, refrigerated drawers and natural teak decking that together support both casual daytime lounging and formal evenings under way.

Performance, Propulsion Systems and Advanced Navigation Tech

Twin inboard MAN V12 1900hp engines (each with approximately 590 hours) drive direct‑drive propulsion backed by a comprehensive technical suite—CMC fin stabilizers for underway and at‑anchor comfort, hydraulic Sleipner bow and stern thrusters, a 3,434‑gallon fuel tank and a 400‑gallon freshwater capacity that support long passages; electronics include dual Garmin GPSMAP 8424 24″ displays, Fantom 126 open‑array radar, autopilot, AIS 800, multiple sonar modules and an integrated CM8 power management system, while two Kohler 32 kW generators, Victron 8 kW Quattro inverters and an HRO Seafari 221 L/hr watermaker provide robust service systems.

Private Staterooms, Guest Cabins and En Suite Details

Accommodation comprises a forward VIP queen and a king‑bed master—both appointed with large windows, Samsung 55″ TVs, surround sound and en suite heads—plus two aft guest cabins (one queen, one twin) with sprung mattresses and individual entertainment systems; en suites feature Tecma Silent Plus macerating toilets, upgraded Storm Gris honed porcelain shower bulkheads and extensive cabinetry and vanity surfaces, while crew access and two crew cabins with a separate mess ensure discreet service and efficient operation.

Key Specifications Recap and How to Learn More

Notable technical highlights include LOA 88.92 ft, beam 23.5 ft, draft 6.08 ft, twin MAN V12 1900 hp engines, 3,434‑gallon fuel capacity, HRO watermaker (221 L/hr), CMC fin stabilization and two Kohler 32 kW generators; for prospective owners this translates into a well‑appointed platform for extended cruising, accessible systems for professional crews and multiple entertaining zones for guests — to review detailed specifications, view additional imagery or arrange a private tour, contact the seller directly.

For more information on this yacht including additional pictures and brochures, or to schedule a tour, please contact us below. While efforts have been made to ensure accuracy, readers are encouraged to verify details independently.
